scope: Birth and death years and places for deceased historical figures. Pins represent settlements or approximate localities rather than claimed exact buildings.

figures.name: Leonardo da Vinci
aliases: Leonardo di ser Piero da Vinci
figures.note: The exact birthplace is uncertain; Anchiano near Vinci is traditional. The birth pin represents the Vinci area. He died at Clos Lucé in Amboise.

figures.name: Michelangelo
figures.note: Caprese is now named Caprese Michelangelo. He died in Rome, although his burial is in Florence.

figures.name: Galileo Galilei
figures.note: Arcetri is now a neighbourhood of Florence; the marker represents the locality, not the exact villa.

figures.name: Isaac Newton
figures.note: Uses Gregorian years: his birth was 25 December 1642 in the contemporary English calendar, or 4 January 1643 Gregorian. He died in Kensington; Westminster Abbey is his burial place.

figures.name: Charles Darwin
figures.note: He died at Down House in Downe, historically Kent and now Greater London. Westminster Abbey is his burial place.

figures.name: Ada Lovelace
figures.note: She died in Marylebone. Both markers represent London at city scale.

figures.name: Marie Curie
figures.note: She died at the Sancellemoz sanatorium in Passy, Haute-Savoie, not the Paris district of Passy or the Panthéon where she was later reinterred.

figures.name: Ludwig van Beethoven
figures.note: His exact birth day is unrecorded, but baptism on 17 December 1770 establishes the birth year.

figures.name: Pablo Picasso
figures.note: He died in Mougins. Vauvenargues, where he was buried, is a different location.

figures.name: Mary Shelley
figures.note: Born in Somers Town and died at Chester Square. Both markers represent London at city scale.

figures.name: George Washington
figures.note: The birth marker represents the Popes Creek estate area, now preserved as a national monument. Birth year uses the modern calendar; the contemporary English date fell in 1731 Old Style.

figures.name: Abraham Lincoln

birth.place: Sinking Spring Farm, near Hodgenville, Kentucky, USA

figures.note: The birth pin represents the preserved farm site, not a claim about the original cabin’s exact footprint. Then in Hardin County, the site is now in LaRue County. He died in Washington, D.C., not at his burial site in Springfield.

sources.title: National Park Service — President Abraham Lincoln

figures.name: Harriet Tubman

birth.place: Dorchester County, near Madison, Maryland, USA

figures.note: Birth is usually dated circa 1822; older accounts give other years, including 1820. The precise birthplace is uncertain. The pin marks the Madison area, not an exact cabin site.

sources.title: National Park Service — Tubman frequently asked questions
National Park Service — determining Tubman’s birth year
Maryland Department of Natural Resources — Tubman timeline

figures.name: Frederick Douglass

birth.place: Tuckahoe area, near Cordova, Maryland, USA

figures.note: 1818 follows the surviving enslaver’s records; Douglass himself did not know his exact birth date. The birth pin represents the Cordova–Tuckahoe area, not the precise cabin site. He died at Cedar Hill in Washington, D.C.; Rochester is his burial place.

figures.name: Frida Kahlo
aliases: Magdalena Carmen Frida Kahlo y Calderón
figures.note: Both pins represent Coyoacán, then a settlement outside central Mexico City and now a city borough. The exact birth house is disputed; the locality and year are established.

figures.name: Simón Bolívar
aliases: Simon Jose Antonio de la Santisima Trinidad Bolivar y Palacios
figures.note: He died at the Quinta de San Pedro Alejandrino near Santa Marta. The pin represents Santa Marta, not his later burial place in Caracas.

figures.name: Srinivasa Ramanujan
figures.note: He died in Chetput, Madras. Some short biographies instead give Kumbakonam, where he grew up.

figures.name: Akira Kurosawa
figures.note: Born in what is now Shinagawa; died in Setagaya. Both markers represent Tokyo.

figures.name: Yasujirō Ozu
figures.note: Born in Fukagawa; died in Bunkyō. Both markers represent Tokyo, not his burial place in Kamakura.

figures.name: Yukio Mishima
figures.note: Born in Yotsuya; died at Ichigaya. Both markers represent Tokyo.

figures.name: Hokusai
figures.note: The birth date is uncertain; 1760 is the conventional birth year.

sources.title: Former Residence of Mao Zedong — Wikipedia
Former Residence of Deng Xiaoping — Wikipedia

figures.name: Ho Chi Minh
figures.note: Uses the generally accepted birth year of 1890; he also used other birth years in different records. The birthplace marker represents Hoàng Trù village.

sources.title: Hoàng Trù historic site — Vietnam tourism database
Hoàng Trù — GeoNames coordinates via Mapcarta

figures.name: José Rizal
aliases: Jose Protasio Rizal Mercado y Alonso Realonda
figures.note: He was executed at Bagumbayan, now Rizal Park in Manila.

figures.name: Benigno Aquino Jr.
figures.note: He was assassinated at Manila International Airport; the marker represents the airport complex.

figures.name: Kim Dae-jung
figures.note: Uses the actual Gregorian birth year of 1924, confirmed by his presidential library; some records give 1925. The birth marker represents Hauido island.

sources.title: Life chronology — Kim Dae-jung Presidential Library & Museum

figures.name: Desmond Tutu
figures.note: Map pins mark settlement centres.

figures.name: Miriam Makeba
figures.note: Born in Prospect township, Johannesburg; pins mark settlement centres.

sources.title: Miriam Makeba — South African History Online

figures.name: Patrice Lumumba
figures.note: Pins mark the villages of birth and execution; Shilatembo is outside Lubumbashi.

figures.name: Kwame Nkrumah
figures.note: Uses the accepted 1909 birth year from Nkrumah's own account. Map pins mark settlement centres.

figures.name: Chinua Achebe
figures.note: Often listed as born in Ogidi, but Achebe specified nearby Nnobi in an interview. The pin follows that account.

sources.title: In search of Chinua Achebe (2) — republished 1983 interview

figures.name: Naguib Mahfouz
figures.note: Agouza is in Giza, within Greater Cairo. Map pins mark the city/district centres.

figures.name: Ibn Khaldun
figures.note: Map pins mark settlement centres.

figures.name: Omar Khayyam
figures.note: Dates follow MacTutor's 1048–1131 chronology. Both are uncertain; Encyclopaedia Iranica discusses an alternative death date around 1123.

sources.title: Omar Khayyam — MacTutor, University of St Andrews

figures.name: Kahlil Gibran
figures.note: Map pins mark settlement centres.

figures.name: Avicenna
figures.note: Birth year is approximate; Afshona is also spelled Afshana. Map pins mark settlement centres.

sources.title: Avicenna Museum at Afshona — Bukhara State Museum

figures.name: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk
figures.note: Birth year is approximate. Salonica was then in the Ottoman Empire; it is now Thessaloniki, Greece.

figures.name: Muhammad Ali
figures.note: Map pins mark settlement centres.

figures.name: Martin Luther King Jr.
figures.note: Map pins mark settlement centres.

figures.name: Malcolm X
figures.note: Map pins mark settlement centres.

figures.name: W. E. B. Du Bois
figures.note: Map pins mark settlement centres.

figures.name: Josephine Baker
figures.note: Map pins mark settlement centres.

figures.name: Gabriela Mistral
figures.note: Died at Hempstead General Hospital on Long Island, not in Chile. Map pins mark settlement centres.

sources.title: Gabriela Mistral — National Library of Chile

figures.name: Mercedes Sosa
figures.note: Map pins mark settlement centres.

figures.name: Socrates
figures.note: Born in the Athenian deme of Alopece; the birth year is approximate. Both pins represent Athens.

figures.name: Plato
figures.note: Commonly dated to 428/427–348/347 BCE; the displayed years are approximate.

figures.name: Aristotle
figures.note: The birth pin marks ancient Stagira near Olympiada, not the modern village of Stagira. Chalkida was ancient Chalcis.

figures.name: Archimedes
figures.note: Ancient dates are approximate; the modern city is also called Siracusa.

figures.name: Julius Caesar
figures.note: Born in Rome and assassinated at the Theatre of Pompey; pins mark the city.

figures.name: Cicero
figures.note: Ancient Arpinum is modern Arpino in Lazio; he was killed while leaving his villa at Formiae, modern Formia. Pins represent these localities.

figures.name: Cleopatra VII
figures.note: Birth is dated to late 70 or early 69 BCE.

figures.name: Augustine of Hippo
figures.note: Ancient Thagaste and Hippo Regius correspond to present-day Souk Ahras and Annaba.

figures.name: Thomas Aquinas
figures.note: Probably born at the castle near Roccasecca, around 1225; died at Fossanova Abbey. The birth pin represents Roccasecca.

figures.name: Petrarch
figures.note: The death village is now named Arquà Petrarca.

figures.name: Joan of Arc
figures.note: The birth year is approximate.

figures.name: Hildegard of Bingen
figures.note: Born around 1098; the pins represent the traditional birth locality and Bingen.

figures.name: Christine de Pizan
figures.note: The death year is approximate.

figures.name: William Shakespeare
figures.note: The precise birthday is unknown; the birth year is documented by his baptism.

figures.name: René Descartes
figures.note: The birthplace is now named Descartes; its historical name is used to avoid giving away the answer.

figures.name: Immanuel Kant
figures.note: The city was Königsberg in Prussia during his lifetime.

figures.name: Mary Wollstonecraft
figures.note: Born in Spitalfields and died in Somers Town; both pins represent London.

figures.name: Catherine the Great
figures.note: Szczecin was called Stettin and was in Prussia at her birth. She died at the Winter Palace.

figures.name: Napoleon Bonaparte
figures.note: Died at Longwood House during exile on Saint Helena; the pin represents Longwood.

figures.name: Giuseppe Garibaldi
figures.note: Died at his home on Caprera; the death pin represents the island, not his exact house.

figures.name: Florence Nightingale
figures.note: Died in Mayfair, London; she was buried elsewhere.

figures.name: Leo Tolstoy
figures.note: Born on the Yasnaya Polyana estate and died at Astapovo railway station. Astapovo is now named Lev Tolstoy; its historical name avoids giving away the answer.

figures.name: Henrik Ibsen
figures.note: Oslo was named Kristiania at his death.

figures.name: Edvard Munch
figures.note: The birth pin represents Ådalsbruk, the village containing his birthplace.

figures.name: Jean Sibelius
figures.note: Died at Ainola, his home in Järvenpää; the pin represents the town.

figures.name: Rosalind Franklin
figures.note: Born in Notting Hill and died in Chelsea; both pins represent London.

figures.name: Alan Turing
figures.note: Born in Maida Vale, London; died at his home in Wilmslow.

figures.name: Nikola Tesla
figures.note: The birth pin represents Smiljan village. He died in the Hotel New Yorker.

figures.name: Michael Faraday
figures.note: Born in Newington Butts, now London; died at Hampton Court, not at his burial place in Highgate.

figures.name: Gregor Mendel
figures.note: His birthplace was then called Heinzendorf bei Odrau.

figures.name: Tycho Brahe
figures.note: Born at Knutstorp Castle in Scania, then Danish territory.

figures.name: Nicolaus Copernicus
figures.note: Toruń and Frombork were also known as Thorn and Frauenburg.

figures.name: Confucius
figures.note: Traditional dates are approximate. The birth marker represents the Qufu area, rather than a claimed exact birthplace.

figures.name: Mencius
figures.note: The dates are conventional estimates; 372 BCE is also commonly given for his birth.

figures.name: Qin Shi Huang
figures.note: He died at Shaqiu palace while travelling. The marker represents its approximate area in present-day Hebei, not his mausoleum near Xi’an.

figures.name: Gautama Buddha
figures.note: Uses the approximate 480–400 BCE chronology. Other traditions place him earlier, including 563–483 BCE. Lumbini and Kushinagar are the traditional birth and death locations.

sources.title: Lumbini, the Birthplace of the Lord Buddha — UNESCO

figures.name: Zhang Heng
figures.note: Born at Xi’e in Nanyang Commandery; the birth marker represents the Nanyang area.

figures.name: Cai Lun
figures.note: His birth year is uncertain, with estimates ranging from about 50 to 62 CE. The marker represents modern Leiyang.

figures.name: Al-Biruni
figures.note: His death is often dated 1048, but some scholars place it around 1050 or later. Kath is represented by modern Beruniy.

figures.name: Abu Bakr al-Razi
aliases: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Zakariya al-Razi
figures.note: Birth is dated 864 or 865; accounts date his death to 925 or 935.

figures.name: Al-Ghazali
figures.note: The birth year is approximate; markers represent historic Tus.

figures.name: Averroes
aliases: Abu al-Walid Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Rushd

figures.name: Toyotomi Hideyoshi
figures.note: Born in Nakamura and died at Fushimi Castle; markers represent their modern cities.

figures.name: Tokugawa Ieyasu
figures.note: Born at Okazaki Castle; died at Sunpu Castle.

figures.name: Yi Sun-sin
figures.note: Killed during the naval Battle of Noryang. The death marker represents the battle area at sea, not a burial site.

figures.name: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman
figures.note: He was assassinated at his home in Dhanmondi, Dhaka.

figures.name: Bhumibol Adulyadej
aliases: ภูมิพลอดุลยเดช

figures.name: Pridi Banomyong
aliases: ปรีดี พนมยงค์
figures.note: He died at his home in Antony, a suburb of Paris.

sources.title: Pridi memorial volume, page90 — Thammasat University

figures.name: Sirimavo Bandaranaike
figures.note: She died at Kadawatha while returning home after voting.

figures.name: Anagarika Dharmapala
figures.note: Colombo is his birthplace; Matara was associated with his father’s family.

sources.title: Karu Jayasuriya’s Dharmapala anniversary address — Sunday Times Sri Lanka

figures.name: Abdus Salam
figures.note: Jhang is the birthplace on his birth certificate. Some accounts instead identify his mother’s village of Santokdas; the birth location is qualified accordingly.

figures.name: Rumi
figures.note: The birth marker follows the tentative identification of medieval Wakhsh with the Sangtuda area, not the modern town of Vakhsh. Other biographies give Balkh, the city with which his family was associated.

sources.title: Franklin Lewis: Rumi, the Icon and the Man — Foundation for Iranian Studies

figures.name: Hafez
figures.note: Uses Encyclopaedia Iranica’s approximate dates; his birth year is variously estimated between about 1315 and 1325.

sources.title: Hafez: Life and times — Encyclopaedia Iranica

figures.name: Umm Kulthum
figures.note: Her birth year is disputed: 1904 and 1898 are both widely reported.

sources.title: The early years — Umm Kulthum Archive

figures.name: Chulalongkorn
aliases: จุฬาลงกรณ์

figures.name: José Martí
figures.note: Died in battle near Dos Ríos; the pin marks the settlement rather than the exact battlefield.

figures.name: José de San Martín
figures.note: 1778 is the conventional birth year; surviving documents disagree about his age.

figures.name: Bernardo O’Higgins
figures.note: Born in the original town of Chillán, now Chillán Viejo.

figures.name: Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz
figures.note: Birth year is debated: 1648 and 1651 both appear in scholarship.

sources.title: Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz — biography

figures.name: Pakal the Great
figures.note: The pins mark the ancient Maya city, not the nearby modern town.

sources.title: Columbia University — Introduction to One Hundred Years of Solitude

figures.name: Rubén Darío
figures.note: His birthplace, Metapa, is now named Ciudad Darío.

figures.name: Augusto César Sandino
figures.note: Killed in the Larreynaga area of Managua.

figures.name: Jomo Kenyatta
figures.note: His birth year is uncertain, commonly given as about 1897. The birth pin marks nearby Gatundu, not the exact rural homestead.

figures.name: Samora Machel
figures.note: Born at Madragoa, now Xilembene (also spelled Chilembene). Killed in an aircraft crash near Mbuzini; the death pin marks the nearby settlement.

sources.title: South African History Online — Samora Machel birthplace

figures.name: Agostinho Neto
figures.note: The birth pin represents the Caxicane village area rather than the exact birthplace.

figures.name: Albert Luthuli
figures.note: His birth year is uncertain; 1898 is the conventional estimate. Stanger is now named KwaDukuza.

figures.name: Habib Bourguiba
figures.note: 1903 is his official birth year; he believed he might have been born in 1901 or 1902.

figures.name: Katherine Mansfield
figures.note: Born in Thorndon, Wellington; died at the Prieuré in Avon, adjoining Fontainebleau.

figures.name: Don Bradman
figures.note: Died at home in Kensington Park, a suburb of Adelaide.

figures.name: Te Puea Hērangi
figures.note: The birth pin marks nearby Pirongia rather than the former Whatiwhatihoe settlement. Died at Tūrangawaewae Farm, Ngāruawāhia.

figures.name: Liliʻuokalani
figures.note: Born in the independent Hawaiian Kingdom; died at Washington Place in Honolulu.

figures.name: Toni Morrison
figures.note: Died in the Bronx, New York City.
